gene.name: alkaline phosphatase, biomineralization associated
gene.function: Alkaline phosphatase that metabolizes various phosphate compounds and plays a key role in skeletal mineralization and adaptive thermogenesis. Has broad substrate specificity and can hydrolyze a considerable variety of compounds: however, only a few substrates, such as diphosphate (inorganic pyrophosphate; PPi), pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) and N- phosphocreatine are natural substrates. Plays an essential role in skeletal and dental mineralization via its ability to hydrolyze extracellular diphosphate, a potent mineralization inhibitor, to phosphate: it thereby promotes hydroxyapatite crystal formation and increases inorganic phosphate concentration. Acts in a non- redundant manner with PHOSPHO1 in skeletal mineralization: while PHOSPHO1 mediates the initiation of hydroxyapatite crystallization in the matrix vesicles (MVs), ALPL/TNAP catalyzes the spread of hydroxyapatite crystallization in the extracellular matrix (By similarity). Also promotes dephosphorylation of osteopontin (SSP1), an inhibitor of hydroxyapatite crystallization in its phosphorylated state; it is however unclear whether ALPL/TNAP mediates SSP1 dephosphorylation via a direct or indirect manner (By similarity). Catalyzes dephosphorylation of PLP to pyridoxal (PL), the transportable form of vitamin B6, in order to provide a sufficient amount of PLP in the brain, an essential cofactor for enzymes catalyzing the synthesis of diverse neurotransmitters. Additionally, also able to mediate ATP degradation in a stepwise manner to adenosine, thereby regulating the availability of ligands for purinergic receptors (By similarity). Also capable of dephosphorylating microbial products, such as lipopolysaccharides (LPS) as well as other phosphorylated small-molecules, such as poly-inosine:cytosine (poly I:C). Acts as a key regulator of adaptive thermogenesis as part of the futile creatine cycle: localizes to the mitochondria of thermogenic fat cells and acts by mediating hydrolysis of N-phosphocreatine to initiate a futile cycle of creatine dephosphorylation and phosphorylation (By similarity). During the futile creatine cycle, creatine and N-phosphocreatine are in a futile cycle, which dissipates the high energy charge of N-phosphocreatine as heat without performing any mechanical or chemical work (By similarity).

gene.name: collagen type I alpha 1 chain
gene.function: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen).

gene.name: cytochrome P450 family 24 subfamily A member 1
gene.function: A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase with a key role in vitamin D catabolism and calcium homeostasis. Via C24- and C23-oxidation pathways, catalyzes the inactivation of both the vitamin D precursor calcidiol (25-hydroxyvitamin D(3)) and the active hormone calcitriol (1-alpha,25-dihydroxyvitamin D(3)). With initial hydroxylation at C-24 (via C24-oxidation pathway), performs a sequential 6-step oxidation of calcitriol leading to the formation of the biliary metabolite calcitroic acid. With initial hydroxylation at C-23 (via C23-oxidation pathway), catalyzes sequential oxidation of calcidiol leading to the formation of 25(OH)D3-26,23-lactone as end product. Preferentially hydroxylates at C-25 other vitamin D active metabolites, such as CYP11A1-derived secosteroids 20S- hydroxycholecalciferol and 20S,23-dihydroxycholecalciferol. Mechanistically, uses molecular oxygen inserting one oxygen atom into a substrate, and reducing the second into a water molecule, with two electrons provided by NADPH via FDXR/adrenodoxin reductase and FDX1/adrenodoxin.

gene.name: cytochrome P450 family 27 subfamily B member 1
gene.function: A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase involved in vitamin D metabolism and in calcium and phosphorus homeostasis. Catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the activation of vitamin D in the kidney, namely the hydroxylation of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3/calcidiol at the C1alpha- position to form the hormonally active form of vitamin D3, 1alpha,25- dihydroxyvitamin D3/calcitriol that acts via the vitamin D receptor (VDR). Has 1alpha-hydroxylase activity on vitamin D intermediates of the CYP24A1-mediated inactivation pathway. Converts 24R,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3/secalciferol to 1-alpha,24,25-trihydroxyvitamin D3, an active ligand of VDR. Also active on 25-hydroxyvitamin D2. Mechanistically, uses molecular oxygen inserting one oxygen atom into a substrate, and reducing the second into a water molecule, with two electrons provided by NADPH via FDXR/adrenodoxin reductase and FDX1/adrenodoxin.

gene.name: cytochrome P450 family 2 subfamily R member 1
gene.function: A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase involved in activation of vitamin D precursors. Catalyzes hydroxylation at C-25 of both forms of vitamin D, vitamin D(2) and D(3) (calciol). Can metabolize vitamin D analogs/prodrugs 1alpha-hydroxyvitamin D(2) (doxercalciferol) and 1alpha-hydroxyvitamin D(3) (alfacalcidol) forming 25-hydroxy derivatives. Mechanistically, uses molecular oxygen inserting one oxygen atom into a substrate, and reducing the second into a water molecule, with two electrons provided by NADPH via cytochrome P450 reductase (CPR; NADPH-ferrihemoprotein reductase).

gene.name: dentin matrix acidic phosphoprotein 1
gene.function: May have a dual function during osteoblast differentiation. In the nucleus of undifferentiated osteoblasts, unphosphorylated form acts as a transcriptional component for activation of osteoblast- specific genes like osteocalcin. During the osteoblast to osteocyte transition phase it is phosphorylated and exported into the extracellular matrix, where it regulates nucleation of hydroxyapatite. .

gene.name: egl-9 family hypoxia inducible factor 1
gene.function: Cellular oxygen sensor that catalyzes, under normoxic conditions, the post-translational formation of 4-hydroxyproline in hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) alpha proteins. Hydroxylates a specific proline found in each of the oxygen-dependent degradation (ODD) domains (N-terminal, NODD, and C-terminal, CODD) of HIF1A. Also hydroxylates HIF2A. Has a preference for the CODD site for both HIF1A and HIF1B. Hydroxylated HIFs are then targeted for proteasomal degradation via the von Hippel-Lindau ubiquitination complex. Under hypoxic conditions, the hydroxylation reaction is attenuated allowing HIFs to escape degradation resulting in their translocation to the nucleus, heterodimerization with HIF1B, and increased expression of hypoxy- inducible genes. EGLN1 is the most important isozyme under normoxia and, through regulating the stability of HIF1, involved in various hypoxia-influenced processes such as angiogenesis in retinal and cardiac functionality. Target proteins are preferentially recognized via a LXXLAP motif.

gene.name: ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1
gene.function: Nucleotide pyrophosphatase that generates diphosphate (PPi) and functions in bone mineralization and soft tissue calcification by regulating pyrophosphate levels (By similarity). PPi inhibits bone mineralization and soft tissue calcification by binding to nascent hydroxyapatite crystals, thereby preventing further growth of these crystals. Preferentially hydrolyzes ATP, but can also hydrolyze other nucleoside 5' triphosphates such as GTP, CTP and UTP to their corresponding monophosphates with release of pyrophosphate, as well as diadenosine polyphosphates, and also 3',5'-cAMP to AMP. May also be involved in the regulation of the availability of nucleotide sugars in the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi, and the regulation of purinergic signaling. Inhibits ectopic joint calcification and maintains articular chondrocytes by repressing hedgehog signaling; it is however unclear whether hedgehog inhibition is direct or indirect (By similarity). Appears to modulate insulin sensitivity and function. Also involved in melanogenesis. Also able to hydrolyze 2',3'-cGAMP (cyclic GMP-AMP), a second messenger that activates TMEM173/STING and triggers type-I interferon production. 2',3'-cGAMP degradation takes place in the lumen or extracellular space, and not in the cytosol where it is produced; the role of 2',3'-cGAMP hydrolysis is therefore unclear. Not able to hydrolyze the 2',3'-cGAMP linkage isomer 3'-3'-cGAMP.

gene.name: erythroferrone
gene.function: Iron-regulatory hormone that acts as an erythroid regulator after hemorrhage: produced by erythroblasts following blood loss and mediates suppression of hepcidin (HAMP) expression in the liver, thereby promoting increased iron absorption and mobilization from stores. Promotes lipid uptake into adipocytes and hepatocytes via transcriptional up- regulation of genes involved in fatty acid uptake (By similarity). Inhibits apoptosis and inflammatory response in cardiomyocytes via promotion of sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) and cAMP-dependent activation of AKT signaling (By similarity). Inhibits autophagy induced by nutrient deficiency in hepatocytes via promoting the phosphorylation of IRS1, AKT, and MTOR, and thereby subsequent activation of the AKT- MTOR signaling pathway (By similarity). Negatively regulates the differentiation of osteoblasts, potentially via sequestering BMP2, and thereby inhibits the activation of SMAD signaling (By similarity). The reduction in BMP2 signaling in osteoblasts also results in an increase in expression of the osteoclastogenesis-promoting factors TNFSF11/RANKL and SOST, thereby indirectly promotes bone resorption (By similarity).

gene.name: FAM20C golgi associated secretory pathway kinase
gene.function: Golgi serine/threonine protein kinase that phosphorylates secretory pathway proteins within Ser-x-Glu/pSer motifs and plays a key role in biomineralization of bones and teeth. Constitutes the main protein kinase for extracellular proteins, generating the majority of the extracellular phosphoproteome. Mainly phosphorylates proteins within the Ser-x-Glu/pSer motif, but also displays a broader substrate specificity. Phosphorylates ERO1A, enhancing its activity which is required to maintain endoplasmic reticulum redox homeostasis and for oxidative protein folding. During endoplasmic reticulum stress, phosphorylates P4HB/PDIA1 which induces a functional switch, causing P4HB to change from an oxidoreductase to a molecular chaperone. This is critical to maintain ER proteostasis and reduce cell death under ER stress. Phosphorylation of P4HB also promotes its interaction with ERN1, leading to reduced activity of ERN1, a key sensor for the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response. Required for osteoblast differentiation and mineralization. Phosphorylates casein as well as a number of proteins involved in biomineralization such as AMELX, AMTN, ENAM and SPP1/OPN. In addition to its role in biomineralization, also plays a role in lipid homeostasis, wound healing and cell migration and adhesion.

gene.name: fibroblast growth factor 2
gene.function: Acts as a ligand for FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3 and FGFR4. Also acts as an integrin ligand which is required for FGF2 signaling. Binds to integrin ITGAV:ITGB3. Plays an important role in the regulation of cell survival, cell division, cell differentiation and cell migration. Functions as a potent mitogen in vitro. Can induce angiogenesis. Mediates phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and thereby promotes retinal lens fiber differentiation.

gene.name: fibroblast growth factor receptor 1
gene.function: Tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, differentiation and migration. Required for normal mesoderm patterning and correct axial organization during embryonic development, normal skeletogenesis and normal development of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neuronal system. Phosphorylates PLCG1, FRS2, GAB1 and SHB. Ligand binding leads to the activation of several signaling cascades. Activation of PLCG1 leads to the production of the cellular signaling molecules diacylglycerol and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. Phosphorylation of FRS2 triggers recruitment of GRB2, GAB1, PIK3R1 and SOS1, and mediates activation of RAS, MAPK1/ERK2, MAPK3/ERK1 and the MAP kinase signaling pathway, as well as of the AKT1 signaling pathway. Promotes phosphorylation of SHC1, STAT1 and PTPN11/SHP2. In the nucleus, enhances RPS6KA1 and CREB1 activity and contributes to the regulation of transcription. FGFR1 signaling is down-regulated by IL17RD/SEF, and by FGFR1 ubiquitination, internalization and degradation.

gene.name: fibroblast growth factor receptor 3
gene.function: Tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation and apoptosis. Plays an essential role in the regulation of chondrocyte differentiation, proliferation and apoptosis, and is required for normal skeleton development. Regulates both osteogenesis and postnatal bone mineralization by osteoblasts. Promotes apoptosis in chondrocytes, but can also promote cancer cell proliferation. Required for normal development of the inner ear. Phosphorylates PLCG1, CBL and FRS2. Ligand binding leads to the activation of several signaling cascades. Activation of PLCG1 leads to the production of the cellular signaling molecules diacylglycerol and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. Phosphorylation of FRS2 triggers recruitment of GRB2, GAB1, PIK3R1 and SOS1, and mediates activation of RAS, MAPK1/ERK2, MAPK3/ERK1 and the MAP kinase signaling pathway, as well as of the AKT1 signaling pathway. Plays a role in the regulation of vitamin D metabolism. Mutations that lead to constitutive kinase activation or impair normal FGFR3 maturation, internalization and degradation lead to aberrant signaling. Over-expressed or constitutively activated FGFR3 promotes activation of PTPN11/SHP2, STAT1, STAT5A and STAT5B. Secreted isoform 3 retains its capacity to bind FGF1 and FGF2 and hence may interfere with FGF signaling.

gene.name: furin, paired basic amino acid cleaving enzyme
gene.function: Ubiquitous endoprotease within constitutive secretory pathways capable of cleavage at the RX(K/R)R consensus motif. Mediates processing of TGFB1, an essential step in TGF-beta-1 activation. Converts through proteolytic cleavage the non-functional Brain natriuretic factor prohormone into its active hormone BNP(1-32). By mediating processing of accessory subunit ATP6AP1/Ac45 of the V-ATPase, regulates the acidification of dense-core secretory granules in islets of Langerhans cells (By similarity).

gene.name: growth differentiation factor 2
gene.function: Potent circulating inhibitor of angiogenesis. Signals through the type I activin receptor ACVRL1 but not other Alks. Signaling through SMAD1 in endothelial cells requires TGF-beta coreceptor endoglin/ENG.

gene.name: hepcidin antimicrobial peptide
gene.function: Liver-produced hormone that constitutes the main circulating regulator of iron absorption and distribution across tissues. Acts by promoting endocytosis and degradation of ferroportin/SLC40A1, leading to the retention of iron in iron-exporting cells and decreased flow of iron into plasma. Controls the major flows of iron into plasma: absorption of dietary iron in the intestine, recycling of iron by macrophages, which phagocytose old erythrocytes and other cells, and mobilization of stored iron from hepatocytes.

gene.name: hypoxia inducible factor 1 subunit alpha
gene.function: Functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the adaptive response to hypoxia. Under hypoxic conditions, activates the transcription of over 40 genes, including erythropoietin, glucose transporters, glycolytic enzymes, vascular endothelial growth factor, HILPDA, and other genes whose protein products increase oxygen delivery or facilitate metabolic adaptation to hypoxia. Plays an essential role in embryonic vascularization, tumor angiogenesis and pathophysiology of ischemic disease. Heterodimerizes with ARNT; heterodimer binds to core DNA sequence 5'-TACGTG-3' within the hypoxia response element (HRE) of target gene promoters (By similarity). Activation requires recruitment of transcriptional coactivators such as CREBBP and EP300. Activity is enhanced by interaction with NCOA1 and/or NCOA2. Interaction with redox regulatory protein APEX1 seems to activate CTAD and potentiates activation by NCOA1 and CREBBP. Involved in the axonal distribution and transport of mitochondria in neurons during hypoxia.

gene.name: matrix extracellular phosphoglycoprotein
gene.function: Promotes renal phosphate excretion and inhibits intestinal phosphate absorption. Promotes bone mineralization by osteoblasts and cartilage mineralization by chondrocytes. Regulates the mineralization of the extracellular matrix of the craniofacial complex, such as teeth, bone and cartilage (By similarity). Promotes dental pulp stem cell proliferation and differentiation.

gene.name: MAS related GPR family member D
gene.function: G protein-coupled receptor that acts as a mediator of peripheral pain and itch sensations. Activated by various ligands, such as beta-alanine, beta-aminoisobutyrate, angiotensin 1-7, alamandine and allantoin, causing a conformation change that triggers signaling via guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) and modulates the activity of downstream effectors. MRGPRD is both coupled to G(q) and G(i) G proteins: G(q) coupling activates phospholipase C-beta, releasing diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) second messengers, while G(i) coupling mediates inhibition of adenylate cyclase activity. MRGPRD is specifically expressed in neurons that innervate the epidermis and acts as a key mediator of skin stimuli, such as itch, pain and mechanical stimuli (By similarity). Required to maintain skin homeostasis in response to irritant dermatitis by initiating a signaling that promotes glutamate release, inhibiting mast cell hyperresponsiveness and skin inflammation (By similarity). Required to prevent cardiomyocyte hypertrophy following activation by alamandine, a decarboxylation product of angiotensin 1-7 (By similarity). Acts as a receptor for allantoin in dorsal root ganglion neurons, eliciting chronic itch (pruritus) (By similarity).

gene.name: phosphate regulating endopeptidase X-linked
gene.function: Peptidase that cleaves SIBLING (small integrin-binding ligand, N-linked glycoprotein)-derived ASARM peptides, thus regulating their biological activity. Cleaves ASARM peptides between Ser and Glu or Asp residues. Regulates osteogenic cell differentiation and bone mineralization through the cleavage of the MEPE-derived ASARM peptide. Promotes dentin mineralization and renal phosphate reabsorption by cleaving DMP1- and MEPE-derived ASARM peptides. Inhibits the cleavage of MEPE by CTSB/cathepsin B thus preventing MEPE degradation.

gene.name: RUNX family transcription factor 2
gene.function: Transcription factor involved in osteoblastic differentiation and skeletal morphogenesis. Essential for the maturation of osteoblasts and both intramembranous and endochondral ossification. CBF binds to the core site, 5'-PYGPYGGT-3', of a number of enhancers and promoters, including murine leukemia virus, polyomavirus enhancer, T- cell receptor enhancers, osteocalcin, osteopontin, bone sialoprotein, alpha 1(I) collagen, LCK, IL-3 and GM-CSF promoters. In osteoblasts, supports transcription activation: synergizes with SPEN/MINT to enhance FGFR2-mediated activation of the osteocalcin FGF-responsive element (OCFRE) (By similarity). Inhibits KAT6B-dependent transcriptional activation.

gene.name: solute carrier family 20 member 1
gene.function: Sodium-phosphate symporter which preferentially transports the monovalent form of phosphate with a stoichiometry of two sodium ions per phosphate ion. May play a role in extracellular matrix and cartilage calcification as well as in vascular calcification. Essential for cell proliferation but this function is independent of its phosphate transporter activity.

gene.name: solute carrier family 20 member 2
gene.function: Sodium-phosphate symporter which preferentially transports the monovalent form of phosphate with a stoichiometry of two sodium ions per phosphate ion. Plays a critical role in the determination of bone quality and strength by providing phosphate for bone mineralization (By similarity). Required to maintain normal cerebrospinal fluid phosphate levels (By similarity). Mediates phosphate-induced calcification of vascular smooth muscle cells (VCMCs) and can functionally compensate for loss of SLC20A1 in VCMCs (By similarity).

gene.name: solute carrier family 24 member 3
gene.function: Calcium, potassium:sodium antiporter that transports 1 Ca(2+) and 1 K(+) in exchange for 4 Na(+).

gene.name: solute carrier family 25 member 3
gene.function: Inorganic ion transporter that transports phosphate or copper ions across the mitochondrial inner membrane into the matrix compartment (By similarity). Mediates proton-coupled symport of phosphate ions necessary for mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation of ADP to ATP (By similarity). Transports copper ions probably in the form of anionic copper(I) complexes to maintain mitochondrial matrix copper pool and to supply copper for cytochrome C oxidase complex assembly. May also play a role in regulation of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) (By similarity).

gene.name: solute carrier family 34 member 1
gene.function: Involved in actively transporting phosphate into cells via Na(+) cotransport in the renal brush border membrane. The cotransport has a Na(+):Pi stoichiometry of 3:1 and is electrogenic (By similarity).

gene.name: solute carrier family 34 member 3
gene.function: Involved in actively transporting phosphate into cells via Na(+) cotransport in the renal brush border membrane. The cotransport has a Na(+):Pi stoichiometry of 2:1 and is electroneutral (By similarity).

gene.name: sclerostin
gene.function: Negative regulator of bone growth that acts through inhibition of Wnt signaling and bone formation. .

gene.name: secreted phosphoprotein 1
gene.function: Major non-collagenous bone protein that binds tightly to hydroxyapatite. Appears to form an integral part of the mineralized matrix. Probably important to cell-matrix interaction. .

gene.name: transforming growth factor beta 1
gene.function: Transforming growth factor beta-1 proprotein: Precursor of the Latency-associated peptide (LAP) and Transforming growth factor beta-1 (TGF-beta-1) chains, which constitute the regulatory and active subunit of TGF-beta-1, respectively.

gene.name: vitamin D receptor
gene.function: Nuclear receptor for calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D3 which mediates the action of this vitamin on cells. Enters the nucleus upon vitamin D3 binding where it forms heterodimers with the retinoid X receptor/RXR. The VDR-RXR heterodimers bind to specific response elements on DNA and activate the transcription of vitamin D3-responsive target genes. Plays a central role in calcium homeostasis (By similarity). Also functions as a receptor for the secondary bile acid lithocholic acid (LCA) and its metabolites.

phenotype.definition: Rapid swelling (edema) of the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, mucosa and submucosal tissues of the skin of the face, normally around the mouth, and the mucosa of the mouth and/or throat, as well as the tongue during a period of minutes to several hours. The swelling can also occur elsewhere, typically in the hands. Angioedema is similar to urticaria, but the swelling is subcutaneous rather than on the epidermis.
A partial or complete breakage of the continuity of a bone.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to bone.
An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a coronary artery.

Craniosynostosis refers to the premature closure of the cranial sutures. Primary craniosynostosis refers to the closure of one or more sutures due to abnormalities in skull development, and secondary craniosynostosis results from failure of brain growth.
Delayed ossification of the femoral head.
phenotype.lay: Delayed maturation of the head of the thigh bone

phenotype.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.
A subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.
Excessive production of parathyroid hormone (PTH) by the parathyroid glands.
The concentration of phosphate ion in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased excretion of phosphates in the urine.
The concentration of phosphate ion in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.
Joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in a joint or joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity. Joint stiffness typically subsides over time.
Exaggerated anterior convexity of the thoracic vertebral column.
Reduced strength of muscles.
A disorder of muscle unrelated to impairment of innervation or neuromuscular junction.
Nephrocalcinosis is the deposition of calcium salts in renal parenchyma.
Kidney stones (calculi) are mineral concretions in the renal calyces and pelvis that are found free or attached to the renal papillae.

Degeneration (wear and tear) of articular cartilage, i.e., of the joint surface. Joint degeneration may be accompanied by osteophytes (bone overgrowth), narrowing of the joint space, regions of sclerosis at the joint surface, or joint deformity.

Osteomalacia is a general term for bone weakness owing to a defect in mineralization of the protein framework known as osteoid. This defective mineralization is mainly caused by lack in vitamin D. Osteomalacia in children is known as rickets.

Osteopenia is a term to define bone density that is not normal but also not as low as osteoporosis. By definition from the World Health Organization osteopenia is defined by bone densitometry as a T score -1 to -2.5.
An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage, or described in terms of such damage.
Calcified deposits in soft tissue structures outside a joint.

A row of beadlike prominences at the junction of a rib and its cartilage (i.e., enlarged costochondral joints), resembling a rosary. Note that rachitic rosary would have one bead per rib (a swelling at the costochondral junction), while beaded ribs in the context of multiple rib fractures have multiple beads (fractures) along the same rib.
Increased susceptibility to dental abscess, as manifested by recurrent episodes of dental abscesses that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.
High urine phosphate in the presence of hypophosphatemia.

Rickets is divided into two major categories including calcipenic and phosphopenic. Hypophosphatemia is described as a common manifestation of both categories. Hypophosphatemic rickets is the most common type of rickets that is characterized by low levels of serum phosphate, resistance to ultraviolet radiation or vitamin D intake. There are several issues involved in hypophosphatemic rickets such as calcium, vitamin D, phosphorus deficiencies. Moreover, other disorder can be associated with its occurrence such as absorption defects due to pancreatic, intestinal, gastric, and renal disorders and hepatobiliary disease. Symptoms are usually seen in childhood and can be varied in severity. Severe forms may be linked to bowing of the legs, poor bone growth, and short stature as well as joint and bone pain. Hypophosphatemic rickets are associated with renal excretion of phosphate, hypophosphatemia, and mineral defects in bones. The familial type of the disease is the most common type of rickets.

phenotype.definition: Secondary hyperparathyroidism refers to the production of higher than normal levels of parathyroid hormone in the presence of hypocalcemia.
A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. Although there is no universally accepted definition of short stature, many refer to "short stature" as height more than 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender (or below the 3rd percentile for age and gender dependent norms).
An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal.
A pocket of pus located within a region of a tooth.

Weakness of the hip girdle and upper thigh muscles, for instance in myopathies, leads to an instability of the pelvis on standing and walking. If the muscles extending the hip joint are affected, the posture in that joint becomes flexed and lumbar lordosis increases. The patients usually have difficulties standing up from a sitting position. Due to weakness in the gluteus medius muscle, the hip on the side of the swinging leg drops with each step (referred to as Trendelenburg sign). The gait appears waddling. The patients frequently attempt to counteract the dropping of the hip on the swinging side by bending the trunk towards the side which is in the stance phase (in the German language literature this is referred to as Duchenne sign). Similar gait patterns can be caused by orthopedic conditions when the origin and the insertion site of the gluteus medius muscle are closer to each other than normal, for instance due to a posttraumatic elevation of the trochanter or pseudarthrosis of the femoral neck.

papers.title: Impact of Early Conventional Treatment on Adult Bone and Joints in a Murine Model of X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In the Hyp mouse model of X-linked hypophosphatemia, early treatment with phosphate and calcitriol improved trabecular bone microarchitecture, growth gains, sclerostin expression, and sacroiliac joint erosions. It did not restore final spine length or osteoid mineralization and had no noticeable effect on calcaneal enthesophytes, while later treatment showed limited efficacy overall.
papers.why: This preclinical study tests conventional phosphorus plus calcitriol therapy in an XLH mouse model and quantifies effects on bone, joint, and enthesopathy outcomes.

papers.title: Burosumab for the Treatment of Tumor-Induced Osteomalacia.
papers.summary: In adults with tumor-induced osteomalacia, burosumab increased serum phosphorus and renal tubular phosphate reabsorption, improved several osteomalacia histomorphometric measures, fracture healing, pain, fatigue, and physical health, and had an acceptable reported safety profile. The paper also identifies burosumab as an approved treatment for X-linked hypophosphatemia and reports that two patients initially enrolled as having tumor-induced osteomalacia were subsequently diagnosed with X-linked hypophosphatemia by PHEX genetic testing.
papers.why: Burosumab improved phosphate metabolism, osteomalacia histomorphometry, fractures, pain, fatigue, and physical health in FGF23-mediated tumor-induced osteomalacia, a closely related disease mechanism.

papers.title: Three-Month Randomized Clinical Trial of Nasal Calcitonin in Adults with X-linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 400 IU/day of nasal salmon calcitonin did not significantly alter FGF23, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, TmP/GFR, or other measured biochemical and bone-turnover outcomes in 21 adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia. The authors contrast this null result with a prior review-level observation that a single subcutaneous dose lowered FGF23 and transiently increased serum phosphate, while suggesting that other approaches to calcitonin receptor signaling might regulate osteocytic FGF23 production.
papers.why: A randomized trial directly tested nasal calcitonin in XLH and provides biochemical, renal phosphate, and bone outcome data, including evidence of lack of efficacy.

papers.title: The Lifelong Impact of X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: Results From a Burden of Disease Survey.
papers.summary: This global cross-sectional survey found that children and adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia retain substantial lifelong morbidity despite common treatment with oral phosphate and active vitamin D, including impaired growth, deformity, fractures, pain, stiffness, reduced mobility, and poor physical health status. The paper also summarizes prior clinical-trial evidence that burosumab, an anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody, normalizes serum phosphorus and improves selected skeletal and functional outcomes in children and adults with XLH.
papers.why: The study reports validated patient-reported pain, stiffness, and physical-function measures and a large XLH survey resource capturing lifelong disease burden.

papers.title: Burosumab Improved Histomorphometric Measures of Osteomalacia in Adults with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: A Phase 3, Single-Arm, International Trial.
papers.summary: In a 48-week, single-arm phase 3 study, burosumab significantly improved osteomalacia histomorphometry in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia, increased serum phosphorus and renal tubular phosphate reabsorption, promoted healing of active pseudofractures, and reduced pain and fatigue. Treatment was associated with frequent adverse events, although most were mild or moderate, and the small uncontrolled study did not directly quantify cortical osteomalacia or compare burosumab with conventional therapy.
papers.why: This phase 3 trial directly demonstrates that burosumab improves phosphate homeostasis and osteomalacia histomorphologic measures in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Excessive Osteocytic Fgf23 Secretion Contributes to Pyrophosphate Accumulation and Mineralization Defect in Hyp Mice.
papers.summary: The paper shows that excessive osteocytic FGF23 secretion in the Hyp mouse model of X-linked hypophosphatemia activates FGFR3-dependent suppression of tissue nonspecific alkaline phosphatase, causing pyrophosphate accumulation and contributing to defective bone mineralization. FGFR3 inhibition, anti-FGF23 antibody treatment, or osteoblast-lineage Fgf23 deletion improved these molecular defects, but signaling inhibition only partially corrected mineralization-related abnormalities.
papers.why: In the Hyp mouse model of XLH, FGF23 blockade or FGFR3 inhibition partially restored mineralization-related measures, providing tested therapeutic strategies and mechanistic assays.

papers.title: Outcome of adult patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia caused by PHEX gene mutations.
papers.summary: This retrospective case-note review of 59 adults with PHEX-associated X-linked hypophosphatemia characterized a heterogeneous mutation set and a high adult burden of skeletal, spinal, dental, renal, and hearing complications. Existing vitamin D and phosphate therapy did not normalize key biochemical measures in this cohort and was associated with increased urinary calcium excretion, while the FGF23-targeting antibody KRN23 remained under investigation and had been reported to improve phosphate-related biochemical abnormalities in cited studies.
papers.why: The 59-adult case-note review provides natural-history outcomes and documents treatment complications and clinically important endpoints for adult XLH.

papers.title: Osteocyte-specific deletion of Fgfr1 suppresses FGF23.
papers.summary: Osteocyte-specific deletion of Fgfr1 in Hyp mice, a mouse homologue of X-linked hypophosphatemia, reduced circulating FGF23 and partially improved hypophosphatemia, vitamin D metabolism, growth, and rickets/osteomalacia. Cell experiments showed that FGFR1 signaling regulates FGF23 at transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels through MAPK/PLCγ and PI3K/Akt-related mechanisms, respectively.
papers.why: Osteocyte-specific Fgfr1 deletion in Hyp mice reduced FGF23 and improved rickets, osteomalacia, serum phosphate, and vitamin D status.

papers.title: Sustained Efficacy and Safety of Burosumab, a Monoclonal Antibody to FGF23, in Children With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In an open-label multicenter study of 52 children aged 5–12 years with X-linked hypophosphatemia, 160 weeks of burosumab improved phosphate reabsorption, serum phosphorus, calcitriol, rickets, lower-limb deformity, growth, mobility, and several patient-function outcomes. Most adverse events were mild to moderate, with no discontinuations, hyperphosphatemia, or clinically meaningful increases in serum calcium, urine calcium excretion, or PTH; 4% of children did not achieve normal serum phosphorus and 8% did not achieve normal TmP/GFR.
papers.why: A 160-week multicenter trial in children with XLH provides direct efficacy and safety data for burosumab and corresponding rickets and phosphate outcomes.

papers.title: Effect of Burosumab Compared With Conventional Therapy on Younger vs Older Children With X-linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a post hoc age-group analysis of a 64-week randomized study, burosumab improved phosphate reabsorption and radiographic outcomes more than phosphate salts plus active vitamin D in children with X-linked hypophosphatemia aged 1–12 years. The analysis did not establish that starting burosumab before age 5 improves growth relative to later initiation, and safety findings included frequent adverse events, dental abscesses in older children, and no discontinuation due to hypersensitivity.
papers.why: A randomized pediatric XLH study compares burosumab with conventional therapy across age groups and shows benefits for rickets, deformity, growth, and alkaline phosphatase.

papers.title: Burosumab treatment in adults with X-linked hypophosphataemia: 96-week patient-reported outcomes and ambulatory function from a randomised phase 3 trial and open-label extension.
papers.summary: In adults with X-linked hypophosphataemia, burosumab produced rapid, sustained improvements from baseline in pain, stiffness, fatigue, and ambulatory function through 96 weeks, with selected changes reaching XLH-specific meaningful-change thresholds. The findings support long-term burosumab as symptomatic treatment, although residual pain may persist from structural osteoarthritis and enthesopathy, and the study could not correlate patient-reported changes with radiographical changes.
papers.why: A randomized phase 3 XLH trial provides long-term evidence that burosumab improves patient-reported symptoms and ambulatory function.

papers.title: Genetic diagnosis of X-linked dominant Hypophosphatemic Rickets in a cohort study: tubular reabsorption of phosphate and 1,25(OH)2D serum levels are associated with PHEX mutation type.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 36 probands clinically diagnosed with hypophosphatemic rickets, sequencing, RT-PCR, and MLPA identified a PHEX mutation in every proband and confirmed X-linked hypophosphatemia. Patients with clearly deleterious PHEX mutations had lower tubular phosphate reabsorption and lower serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels, while most other genotype-phenotype comparisons were not statistically significant; the associations require confirmation in larger cohorts.
papers.why: The study provides a genetic diagnostic workflow and shows that tubular phosphate reabsorption and calcitriol levels distinguish deleterious from likely causative PHEX variants.

papers.title: Health-related quality of life and a cost-utility simulation of adults in the UK with osteogenesis imperfecta, X-linked hypophosphatemia and fibrous dysplasia.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional observational study measured health-related quality of life in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia, osteogenesis imperfecta, and fibrous dysplasia. XLH participants had relatively high mean health utility and visual analogue scores, while pain/discomfort and mobility were prominent problems; the cost-utility simulation was conducted only for osteogenesis imperfecta and does not provide evidence of benefit for XLH.
papers.why: The study measured adult XLH quality of life with EQ-5D-5L and demonstrated a method for estimating treatment-related willingness to pay in rare bone disease.

papers.title: The International X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH) Registry: first interim analysis of baseline demographic, genetic and clinical data.
papers.summary: The first interim analysis of the International XLH Registry provides real-world baseline data from 579 people with X-linked hypophosphatemia, confirming a high prevalence of PHEX variants and documenting skeletal, dental, renal, joint, growth, and fracture manifestations across childhood and adulthood. Mechanistic and treatment statements describe pathological FGF23 activity as a central driver of phosphate wasting and burosumab as an anti-FGF23 therapy, but this interim publication does not report treatment efficacy or safety outcomes.
papers.why: The international registry supplies a large longitudinal-ready resource containing PHEX, diagnostic, demographic, auxologic, and clinical data for XLH.

papers.title: Effect of four monthly doses of a human monoclonal anti-FGF23 antibody (KRN23) on quality of life in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In an open-label Phase 1/2 dose-escalation study, adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia received up to four subcutaneous doses of KRN23, a human monoclonal antibody directed at FGF23. SF-36v2 and WOMAC were supported as instruments for assessing health-related quality of life in XLH, with significant improvement after KRN23 in SF-36v2 Role Limitations due to Physical Health and WOMAC Physical Functioning and Stiffness scores, although the quality-of-life analyses were exploratory, small-sample, and open-label.
papers.why: A phase 1/2 XLH study evaluated KRN23 treatment and validated the SF-36v2 and WOMAC instruments for measuring disease-related quality of life.

papers.title: Clinical Evidence for the Benefits of Burosumab Therapy for X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH) and Other Conditions in Adults and Children.
papers.summary: This review reports that burosumab, an FGF23-neutralizing antibody, improves phosphate regulation, rickets, bone mineralization, pain, physical function, growth, and fracture healing in adults and children with X-linked hypophosphatemia, outperforming conventional phosphate/calcitriol therapy in a pediatric trial. Benefits appear substantial, but long-term safety remains uncertain because chronic or lifelong effects on calcification are unresolved, and treatment was associated with more adverse events and increased pediatric dental abscesses.
papers.why: This review synthesizes clinical-trial evidence for burosumab in pediatric and adult XLH, including efficacy, dosing, safety, and longer-term monitoring considerations.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of a human monoclonal anti-FGF23 antibody (KRN23) in the first multiple ascending-dose trial treating adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia, repeated subcutaneous KRN23 produced dose-exposure-related increases in serum inorganic phosphorus, TmP/GFR, and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, with transient stimulation of bone-turnover markers and no meaningful change in calcium or parathyroid hormone. The findings support KRN23-mediated FGF23 blockade as a promising treatment strategy, although the short study did not demonstrate correction of skeletal disease or secondary hyperparathyroidism.
papers.why: This first-in-human multiple-dose trial provides pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and dose-response data for an anti-FGF23 antibody in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Patient-Reported Complications, Symptoms, and Experiences of Living With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Across the Life-Course.
papers.summary: This multinational qualitative survey of 209 adults and 86 children/adolescents with self-reported or proxy-reported X-linked hypophosphatemia found that its most disruptive manifestations change with age: skeletal pathology predominates in children and adolescents, whereas pain predominates in adults. The study also documents substantial functional, emotional, social, dental, and treatment burdens, including adverse experiences with conventional medication and surgery, limited access to appropriate treatment, and reports of benefit from surgery, activity, and psychological coping strategies.
papers.why: The large multinational survey provides reusable patient-reported outcome domains and qualitative methods for characterizing XLH burden across the life course.

papers.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes from a Randomized, Active-Controlled, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial of Burosumab Versus Conventional Therapy in Children with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a phase 3 trial of children aged 5–12 years with X-linked hypophosphatemia, switching from conventional therapy to burosumab was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in patient-reported pain interference and fatigue through week 64, and significant improvement in PROMIS pain interference versus continued conventional therapy at week 40. Burosumab also significantly improved SF-10 physical health scores from baseline through week 64, although between-treatment differences for several patient-reported outcomes were not statistically significant.
papers.why: A phase 3 randomized trial directly assesses burosumab in pediatric XLH and provides patient-reported outcome measures for pain, function, fatigue, and physical health.

papers.title: The international X-linked hypophosphataemia (XLH) registry (NCT03193476): rationale for and description of an international, observational study.
papers.summary: This paper describes the rationale, design, and intended uses of an international observational registry designed to collect longitudinal real-world data on the natural history, treatment, outcomes, and safety of X-linked hypophosphatemia in paediatric and adult patients. It also reviews XLH pathophysiology and existing treatment evidence, including FGF23 inhibition by burosumab, but reports no new clinical efficacy or safety results from the registry.
papers.why: The paper establishes an international XLH registry and specifies longitudinal clinical, treatment, and safety data that can accelerate research and clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Burosumab and Dental Abscesses in Children With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a monocentric retrospective observational study of 71 children with X-linked hypophosphatemia, burosumab was associated with fewer dental abscesses per month of follow-up than conventional treatment, including in a matched analysis of 19 children treated with both regimens. Burosumab was not associated with a significant reduction in odontogenic facial cellulitis or dental caries, and the retrospective design, treatment-selection bias, group age differences, and limited number of young burosumab-treated children constrain causal conclusions.
papers.why: The retrospective pediatric study reports an association between burosumab and fewer dental abscesses than conventional treatment in XLH.

papers.title: Novel PHEX gene locus-specific database: Comprehensive characterization of vast number of variants associated with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH).
papers.summary: The paper establishes PHEX LSDB, a public locus-specific database containing 870 unique PHEX variants associated with X-linked hypophosphatemia and integrating variant interpretations with clinical and biochemical phenotype data. It characterizes the variant spectrum, reports functional evidence for selected missense variants, finds no reliable genotype–phenotype correlation by serum phosphorus, and describes molecular diagnosis and disease-modifying approaches.
papers.why: The paper establishes a publicly searchable database of 870 PHEX variants with genotype-phenotype information, variant submission, and clinical-trial-informed interpretation.

papers.title: PHEX gene mutations and genotype-phenotype analysis of Korean patients with hypophosphatemic rickets.
papers.summary: Mutational analysis identified eight PHEX variants, including five novel variants, in nine of 15 unrelated Korean patients with hypophosphatemic rickets, and two predicted splice-disrupting variants. Clinical comparison found a trend toward more severe skeletal disease with C-terminal PHEX mutations but no significant associations with mutation type, sex-based gene dosage, or dental-disease severity, and the small cohort limited prognostic conclusions.
papers.why: Direct PHEX sequencing in Korean XLH patients identified eight mutations, including five novel mutations, and assessed mutation-type and location-related phenotype patterns.

papers.title: Approach to Hypophosphatemic Rickets.
papers.summary: This review describes the FGF23-mediated mechanism, diagnostic evaluation, and management of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH), including conventional calcitriol plus oral phosphate therapy and the anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody burosumab. It reports improved phosphate metabolism, rickets, pain, function, mobility, and fracture healing with burosumab, but persistent or uncertain benefits for some skeletal and dental outcomes and important risks from conventional therapy.
papers.why: It provides an evaluation framework and reports established diagnostic and treatment options specifically for hypophosphatemic rickets, including XLH.

papers.title: Molecular Diagnoses of X-Linked and Other Genetic Hypophosphatemias: Results From a Sponsored Genetic Testing Program.
papers.summary: A sponsored 13-gene next-generation sequencing program identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic PHEX variants in 519 of 831 unrelated individuals, including 260 of 319 with a provider-reported clinical XLH diagnosis. The study also identified alternative genetic diagnoses, 65 novel PHEX variants, recurrent PHEX copy-number variants that would often be missed by traditional microarray analysis, and improved variant reclassification through cascade testing and segregation analysis.
papers.why: A large sponsored testing program demonstrates a high-yield NGS diagnostic workflow for XLH and related genetic hypophosphatemias, including detection of copy-number variants.

papers.title: Benefit of burosumab in adults with X-linked hypophosphataemia (XLH) is maintained with long-term treatment.
papers.summary: In adults with X-linked hypophosphataemia, continued burosumab treatment for 48 weeks maintained improvements in phosphate metabolism, patient-reported pain, stiffness, physical function and fatigue, and 6-minute walk distance. An exploratory, non-randomised analysis suggested that these benefits diminish during treatment interruption and return after burosumab is reinstated, although the small, confounded analysis could not establish effects on clinical fractures or pseudofractures.
papers.why: This phase III extension provides direct evidence that continued burosumab sustains biochemical, patient-reported, functional, and ambulatory benefits in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Clinical guidelines for burosumab in the treatment of XLH in children and adolescents: British paediatric and adolescent bone group recommendations.
papers.summary: This guideline paper identifies pathogenic PHEX variants and elevated FGF23 as central to the pathophysiology of X-linked hypophosphataemia (XLH), and recommends burosumab for children and adolescents with radiographic bone disease. It summarizes clinical evidence that burosumab inhibits FGF23, improves phosphate homeostasis and skeletal outcomes, and provides dosing, laboratory monitoring, and safety recommendations for its use in growing patients.
papers.why: This pediatric XLH guideline summarizes evidence for FGF23 inhibition with burosumab and provides a reusable management and monitoring pathway.

papers.title: Growth Curves for Children with X-linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: Pooling pretreatment data from four studies, the paper constructed XLH-specific height-for-age growth curves for 228 children and showed that annual height growth began to diverge from population norms by 6 months, declined markedly by approximately 1 year, and remained deficient through age 12. These reference curves may support evaluation of growth outcomes from therapeutic interventions in pediatric XLH.
papers.why: The pooled longitudinal data provide validated disease-specific growth curves that can serve as natural-history benchmarks for pediatric XLH trials.

papers.title: Diagnosis and management of X-linked hypophosphatemia in children and adolescent in the Gulf Cooperation Council countries.
papers.summary: This guideline identifies PHEX loss-of-function mutations and excess FGF23 signaling as the core mechanism of X-linked hypophosphatemia, leading to renal phosphate wasting, low 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, impaired growth-plate mineralization, and multisystem disease. It provides diagnostic approaches and reports that burosumab, which inhibits FGF23, improves phosphate control, biochemical abnormalities, rickets, deformity, growth, and mobility, while conventional phosphate plus active vitamin D treatment has incomplete efficacy and substantial adverse effects and adherence problems.
papers.why: This disease-specific guideline provides a reusable diagnostic pathway and recommends conventional and anti-FGF23 treatments for pediatric and adolescent XLH.

papers.title: Dental health of pediatric patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) after three years of burosumab therapy.
papers.summary: In a three-year prospective observational study of 10 children and adolescents with X-linked hypophosphatemia, burosumab normalized serum phosphate, healed rickets, and improved height during the first year, with skeletal and growth benefits maintained through year three. Burosumab did not normalize the characteristic excessive pulp dimensions, and recurrent dental abscesses persisted in one patient despite improved phosphate levels, supporting a persistent role for local PHEX-related mineralization inhibitors such as osteopontin.
papers.why: Prospective longitudinal data in children with XLH directly evaluate an existing burosumab treatment and provide dental, radiographic, laboratory, and growth assessment methods and outcomes.

papers.title: Positive Response to One-Year Treatment With Burosumab in Pediatric Patients With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a five-child observational case series of genetically confirmed pediatric X-linked hypophosphatemia, one year of burosumab normalized serum phosphate, increased renal phosphate reabsorption, reduced alkaline phosphatase, and improved growth in three prepubertal children. Treatment was generally well tolerated without serious adverse effects or new nephrocalcinosis, although growth did not improve in two pubertal patients and the small cohort limits generalization and long-term conclusions.
papers.why: One year of burosumab treatment in five children with genetically confirmed XLH improved phosphate reabsorption, biochemical abnormalities, and growth with data from routine clinical practice.

papers.title: Burosumab for X-linked hypophosphatemia in children and adolescents: Opinion based on early experience in seven European countries.
papers.summary: This expert-opinion review reports early European experience and summarizes clinical-trial evidence that burosumab improves phosphate homeostasis and rickets in children and adolescents with X-linked hypophosphatemia. It recommends early, age-adjusted treatment with phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, renal phosphate handling, imaging, and clinical monitoring, while emphasizing that evidence for treatment throughout adolescence and after growth cessation remains limited.
papers.why: The report formulates a clinically tested framework for selecting, dosing, titrating, and monitoring burosumab in pediatric XLH.

papers.title: Long-term Burosumab Administration Is Safe and Effective in Adults With X-linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a long-term, open-label extension study, burosumab increased serum phosphate and renal phosphate reabsorption, improved phosphate-related metabolic and bone-turnover measures, reduced pain, and improved mobility in 20 adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia. Treatment was generally well tolerated, although one life-threatening serious adverse event was considered possibly related and long-term effects on bone healing and osteoarthritis or enthesopathy progression were not established.
papers.why: The long-term extension study directly reports sustained biochemical, biomarker, patient-reported, and mobility benefits with burosumab in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Slc20a1/Pit1 and Slc20a2/Pit2 are essential for normal skeletal myofiber function and survival.
papers.summary: The paper shows that skeletal-muscle Pit1 and Pit2 are jointly required for normal myofiber function and survival: their combined deletion causes severe energy-stress myopathy and early death, while partial loss produces a gene-dose-dependent reduction in running endurance. The findings identify phosphate transport, ERK1/2 signaling, and AMPK-associated mitochondrial metabolism as mechanistic targets that may inform treatment of hypophosphatemic myopathy, including the muscle dysfunction seen in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
papers.why: The study develops phosphate-transporter mouse and myoblast models with hypophosphatemic muscle phenotypes and quantitative functional assays relevant to XLH-related muscle dysfunction.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of 15 families with hereditary hypophosphatemia: Novel Mutations in PHEX and SLC34A3.
papers.summary: In 23 patients from 15 unrelated Turkish families with hereditary hypophosphatemia, PHEX mutations were the predominant genetic finding and were identified in 20 patients from 12 families, including six novel and six de novo variants. The study also identified compound-heterogeneous SLC34A3 variants, demonstrated exon 14 skipping caused by PHEX c.1586+2T>G, and documented clinical responses to calcitriol plus phosphate in patients with PHEX-related or genetically unresolved hypophosphatemic rickets.
papers.why: The study provides a broad genetic testing workflow for hereditary hypophosphatemia that detects PHEX sequence variants, copy-number changes, and phenotypically informative cases.

papers.title: Seven novel and six de novo PHEX gene mutations in patients with hypophosphatemic rickets.
papers.summary: Genetic analysis of 43 patients from 18 unrelated Chinese families identified 17 PHEX mutations, including seven novel mutations and six likely de novo mutations, supporting the major causal role of PHEX in X-linked hypophosphatemia. Serum FGF23 showed wide variation and overlapped substantially with healthy controls, giving it limited diagnostic value for XLH, whereas direct PHEX sequencing supported genetic confirmation of suspected cases.
papers.why: The study applies PHEX sequencing to a 43-patient cohort and evaluates FGF23 as a diagnostic biomarker while identifying novel and de novo mutations.

papers.title: X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Management in Adults: An International Working Group Clinical Practice Guideline.
papers.summary: This guideline identifies excess FGF23-driven renal phosphate wasting as the central mechanism of adult X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) and supports combined clinical, laboratory, radiographic, and PHEX-based genetic assessment. It recommends burosumab particularly for adults with fractures or pseudofractures, while conventional phosphate plus active vitamin D remains an alternative; neither therapy has demonstrated prevention or reversal of enthesopathy or osteoarthritis, and several patient-reported and dental outcomes are uncertain or null.
papers.why: This evidence-based guideline provides diagnostic criteria, monitoring recommendations, and graded management evidence showing burosumab benefits fracture and pseudofracture healing in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Body composition and cardiometabolic health of pediatric patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) under burosumab therapy.
papers.summary: In a small observational study of seven children and adolescents with X-linked hypophosphatemia, one year of burosumab therapy was associated with increased fat-free and appendicular skeletal muscle mass, improved linear growth, and improved radiographic rickets severity. Fat mass did not change significantly, and longer studies are needed to determine whether the favorable body-composition effects persist and affect cardiometabolic outcomes.
papers.why: Own observational data show that burosumab is paired with reusable BIA body-composition measurements and the Thacher Rickets Severity Score to quantify treatment response in pediatric XLH.

papers.title: Dental management of patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: This case report describes the renal phosphate-wasting and dentin defects associated with X-linked hypophosphatemia and documents endodontic and implant outcomes in two affected patients. Conservative root canal treatment produced bone healing without symptoms in one patient, whereas the treated tooth and implants remained hypermobile in the other, underscoring the need for early diagnosis, preventive dental care, and cautious treatment planning.
papers.why: This case report provides direct evidence for endodontic management of XLH-associated periapical abscesses and describes dental monitoring and care coordination.

papers.title: Burosumab in X-linked hypophosphatemia: a profile of its use in the USA.
papers.summary: Burosumab inhibits excess FGF23 activity in X-linked hypophosphatemia, increasing renal and gastrointestinal phosphate absorption, serum phosphorus, calcitriol, and bone mineralization while reducing renal phosphate loss. Clinical studies report improvements in pediatric rickets and adult pain, stiffness, physical function, and fracture healing, although some outcomes such as the adult 6-minute walk test and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase did not improve significantly.
papers.why: Describes burosumab's mechanism, approval, and clinical benefits in increasing serum phosphate and improving rickets and fractures in X-linked hypophosphatemia.

papers.title: Development of Enthesopathies and Joint Structural Damage in a Murine Model of X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In a 12-month longitudinal study, B6.Cg-Phex Hyp/J mice reproduced and progressively developed major structural manifestations of X-linked hypophosphatemia, including enthesophytes, osteoarthritis, joint erosions, periarticular calcifications, and kyphosis. Micro-computed tomography, histology, and immunostaining characterized the natural history and revealed altered osteopontin and sclerostin expression, supporting the model's use for studying XLH mechanisms and therapies.
papers.why: This work validates a mouse model and longitudinal imaging and histology platform for studying XLH-related enthesopathies and joint structural damage.

papers.title: Burosumab vs conventional therapy in children with X-linked hypophosphatemia: results of the open-label, phase 3 extension period.
papers.summary: In children with X-linked hypophosphatemia, continued burosumab through week 88 maintained or sustained improvements in rickets, lower-limb deformity, phosphate metabolism, and growth measures. Crossover from conventional therapy to burosumab produced rapid improvement in phosphate metabolism and rickets healing over 22 weeks, with no new safety signals, although the small nonpowered subgroup limits comparisons.
papers.why: This pediatric phase 3 extension reports treatment efficacy, safety and standardized radiographic, growth and biochemical outcomes for burosumab in XLH.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of 153 Chinese Patients With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study characterized the clinical, biochemical, and mutational features of 153 Chinese patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia and measured serum intact FGF23 in 62 patients. It found broad iFGF23 elevation but no significant correlation with disease severity, age, or PHEX mutation class/location, and no significant biochemical improvement was detected during a limited follow-up of conventional phosphate plus calcitriol therapy.
papers.why: A 153-patient XLH cohort provides concrete PHEX genotyping and serum FGF23 biomarker data that can support molecular diagnosis and research stratification.

papers.title: Lower limb bone geometry in adult individuals with X-linked hypophosphatemia: an observational study.
papers.summary: This observational MRI study found substantial lower-limb skeletal abnormalities in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia, including reduced femoral and tibial torsion, increased femoral bowing and acetabular geometry, altered alignment, and region-specific changes in bone cross-sectional area. The findings provide objective measures for characterizing deformities and planning corrective surgery, although the small cohort and prior lower-limb surgery limit interpretation of natural disease geometry.
papers.why: This study validates quantitative MRI-based bone geometry measures for documenting clinically relevant lower-limb abnormalities in XLH.

papers.title: Dental impact of anti-fibroblast growth factor 23 therapy in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
papers.summary: In young male Hyp mice, weekly FGF23-neutralizing antibody treatment improved dentin, pulp, periodontal, cementum, and alveolar-bone abnormalities, with the 16 mg·kg−1 dose producing near-wild-type rescue of several dentoalveolar features. Retrospective observations in two patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia receiving burosumab were consistent with improved pulp-chamber and mandibular-bone features, but dentin density and some extracellular-matrix abnormalities were not corrected in mice, and longer clinical confirmation is still needed.
papers.why: Tests an FGF23-neutralizing antibody in the Hyp mouse model and reports improved dentin, cementum, alveolar bone, and periodontal findings relevant to XLH dental disease.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Burosumab in Pediatric Patients With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: A Phase 3/4 Open-Label Trial.
papers.summary: In a 124-week open-label phase 3/4 study of 15 Japanese children aged 1–12 years with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH), subcutaneous burosumab increased serum phosphorus and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, decreased alkaline phosphatase, improved rickets radiographic and severity scores, and showed a trend toward improved 6-minute walk-test distance. No apparent change in growth rate was observed, and the study reported an acceptable safety profile without new safety concerns, although its small single-arm design limits causal comparison.
papers.why: This phase 3/4 trial directly validates burosumab efficacy and safety in pediatric XLH while providing biochemical, radiographic, functional, and safety endpoints.

papers.title: New Developments in the Treatment of X-Linked Hypophosphataemia: Implications for Clinical Management.
papers.summary: This review describes PHEX-associated X-linked hypophosphataemia as an FGF23-excess disorder causing renal phosphate wasting, reduced calcitriol production, defective growth-plate and bone mineralisation, and rickets or osteomalacia. It reports that burosumab improves phosphate reabsorption and clinical, biochemical, radiological, growth, fracture-healing, pain, and functional outcomes, while noting unresolved long-term benefits and limited evidence for adjunctive growth hormone, cinacalcet, and calcitonin.
papers.why: Reviews established XLH treatments and clinical monitoring approaches, highlighting burosumab as a therapy targeting FGF23 excess.

papers.title: Renal Phosphate Handling: Independent Effects of Circulating FGF23, PTH, and Calcium.
papers.summary: This clinical study found that circulating FGF23, PTH, and ionized calcium independently lower renal phosphate reabsorption threshold, with PTH status modifying the magnitude of the FGF23 effect. In one patient with X-linked hypophosphatemia and hypoparathyroidism, 28 days of teriparatide markedly lowered TmP/GFR and increased NcAMP and bone-turnover markers, providing evidence that PTH deficiency can attenuate the phosphaturic effect of FGF23 excess.
papers.why: Provides new XLH patient data linking FGF23, PTH, calcium, and TmP/GFR, and tests a parathyroid-directed intervention in hypoparathyroidism.

papers.title: FGF23 directly inhibits osteoprogenitor differentiation in Dmp1-knockout mice.
papers.summary: This paper shows in a Dmp1-knockout mouse model of autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets (ARHR) that osteoblast-lineage Fgf23 deletion normalizes serum phosphate but only partially restores bone growth and mineralization. In vitro and transcriptomic results indicate that FGF23 excess directly inhibits osteoprogenitor differentiation, whereas DMP1 deficiency independently impairs mineralization, supporting combined FGF23 blockade and DMP1 repletion as a potential ARHR therapy and providing mechanistic support for FGF23-directed approaches used in X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH).
papers.why: Tests phosphate repletion and bone-specific FGF23 deletion in a genetically related FGF23-excess rickets model and identifies combined FGF23/DMP1 targeting as a potential strategy.

papers.title: Disease Manifestations and Complications in Dutch X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Patients.
papers.summary: This nationwide observational cohort of 80 Dutch patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) found frequent adiposity, hearing loss, skeletal deformity, osteoarthritis, nephrocalcinosis, and hyperparathyroidism. Earlier XLH-related treatment was associated with greater height but also with earlier and more frequent nephrocalcinosis; the study also characterized FGF23, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D, and bone-turnover abnormalities and their clinical associations.
papers.why: The nationwide registry supplies an XLH cohort and longitudinal clinical outcomes useful for natural history, complication surveillance, and treatment research.

papers.title: Open Label Study of KRN23 on Osteomalacia in Adults With X-linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to establish the effect of KRN23 treatment on improvement in XLH-associated osteomalacia as determined by osteoid volume (osteoid volume/bone volume, OV/BV).

papers.title: Calcitonin for Treating X-linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary:
X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) is the most common form of inherited rickets in the United States. It also causes bone disease in adults. XLH is caused by overproduction of a hormone call FGF23, which makes the body waste phosphate. This study is designed to determine if nasal calcitonin, an already approved drug in the US, can lower blood levels of FGF23 and reduce phosphate wasting in patients with XLH. In this study the investigators will:

1. Determine whether nasal calcitonin significantly lowers integrated 24-hour blood levels of FGF23 in patients with XLH.

papers.title: Burosumab in Children and Adolescents With X-linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary:
In this prospective longitudinal cohort study we studied the efficacy and safety of burosumab in real-clinical practice for \<13- and \>13-years old children affected with X-linked hypophosphatemia.

57 children with XLH were switched from conventional treatment to burosumab. After 12 months we assessed the efficacy and safety of treatment with burosumab on the whole cohort and separately on the cohort of \>13-years old adolescents.

papers.title: Effect of Cinacalcet on Parathyroid Hormone Secretion in Children and Adolescents With Hypophosphatemic Rickets
papers.summary: This study will measure the effect of cinacalcet (Sensipar) on parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion in children and adolescents with hypophosphatemic rickets (XLH). The investigators are seeking evidence that patients with XLH may benefit from treatment with cinacalcet by achieving better control of PTH secretion.

papers.title: A First-in-human Study of KK8123 in Adults With X-linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: A first-in-human study of KK8123 in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia.

papers.title: An Extension Study of KRN23 in Adults With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: The primary purpose of this study is to assess the safety and efficacy of repeated subcutaneous (SC) injections of KRN23 in adult subjects with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH).

papers.title: Prevention of Spontaneous Dental Abscesses in Children With X-linked Hypophosphatemia : a RCT
papers.summary: This study is a prospective, randomized, single-blind, split-mouth, national multicenter trial, comparing the efficacy of a self-etch adhesive system combined (SAM) with a flowable composite to that of a fluoride varnish for the prevention of spontaneous dental abscesses in children with XLH. For each patient, according to randomization, one side of the oral cavity is treated with the experimental treatment (application of the adhesive system to healthy anterior and posterior temporary teeth, and application of the flowable composite to healthy posterior temporary teeth), and the other side wi

papers.title: Anti-FGF23 (Burosumab) in Adult Patients With XLH
papers.summary:
X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) rare genetic disorder due by inactivating mutations in the PHEX gene leading to increased levels in FGF-23. Elevated FGF-23 reduces renal phosphate reabsorbtion and and limits 1-alpha hydroxylase driven Vitamin D activation, eventually leading to phosphate wasting, defective bone mineralization and additional health issues.

Burosumab is a recombinant fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody developed to treat XLH by binding FGF23, thereby restoring normal phosphate homeostasis.

papers.title: Study to Assess the Safety, Pharmacokinetics and Efficacy of KRN23 in Adult Chinese Patients With XLH
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of KRN23 in adult Chinese patients with XLH

papers.title: Study of KRN23 (Burosumab), a Recombinant Fully Human Monoclonal Antibody Against Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF23), in Pediatric Subjects With X-linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)
papers.summary:
The objectives of the study are to:

* Identify a dose and dosing regimen of burosumab, based on safety and pharmacodynamic (PD) effect, in pediatric XLH participants
* Establish the safety profile of burosumab for the treatment of children with XLH including ectopic mineralization risk, cardiovascular effects, and immunogenicity profile
* Characterize the pharmacokinetic (PK)/PD profile of the KRN23 doses tested in the monthly (Q4) and biweekly (Q2) dose regimens in pediatric XLH patients
* Determine the PD effects of burosumab treatment on markers of bone health in pediatric XLH patients
