papers.title: Study to Assess the Safety, Pharmacokinetics and Efficacy of KRN23 in Pediatric Chinese Patients With XLH
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of KRN23 in pediatric Chinese patients with XLH

papers.title: Study of the Anti-FGF23 Antibody, Burosumab, in Adults With XLH
papers.summary: This is phase 3b open-label, international, multicenter study to continue to monitor the long-term safety and efficacy of burosumab in adult patients with XLH that participated in previous clinical trials with burosumab (UX023-CL303 / UX023-CL304).

papers.title: Examining the Effect of Burosumab on Muscle Function
papers.summary: Patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) often report symptoms of fatigue and weakness particularly after exertion, in addition to their skeletal complaints. In previous trials using KRN23 (same drug as burosumab/Crysvita®), patients report these symptoms improve. The investigators wish to test this hypothesis directly by measuring muscle energy when patients begin treatment with Crysvita® for the first time.

papers.title: Calcitriol Monotherapy for X-Linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: Children and adults with XLH recruited will be treated with calcitriol alone (without phosphate supplementation) for one year, during which the calcitriol dose will be escalated during the first 3 months of therapy. The investigators hypothesize that treatment of adults and children with XLH alone will improve serum phosphate levels and skeletal mineralization without causing an increase in kidney calcifications. The study will also examine if calcitriol therapy will improve growth in children.

papers.title: Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Efficacy of Burosumab in Patients Less Than 1 Year of Age
papers.summary: A Phase 1/2, Open-label, Multicenter, Non-randomized Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Efficacy of Burosumab in Paediatric Patients from Birth to Less than 1 Year of Age with X-linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)

papers.title: Study of the Safety, Pharmacodynamics (PD) and Efficacy of KRN23 in Children From 1 to 4 Years Old With X-linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)
papers.summary:
The primary objectives of the study are to:

* Establish the safety profile of KRN23 for the treatment of XLH in children between 1 and 4 years old
* Determine the PD effects of KRN23 treatment on serum phosphorus and other PD markers that reflect the status of phosphate homeostasis in children between 1 and 4 years old with XLH

papers.title: Using Different Doses of Active Vitamin D Combined With Neutral Phosphate in Children With X-linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) is the most common form of heritable rickets. Current treatments include active vitamin D metabolites (e.g. calcitriol) and phosphate salts. There is no consistent weight-based dosing of calcitriol and phosphate now. The primary objective of this study is to establish the efficacy of different dose of calcitriol combined with neutral phosphate in children with XLH.

papers.title: Long-Term Extension Study of KRN23 in Adult Subjects With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)
papers.summary:
The primary objectives of this study are to:

* Assess the long-term safety of KRN23 subcutaneous (SC) administration in adult subjects with XLH
* Assess the proportion of subjects achieving serum phosphorus levels in the normal range (2.5-4.5 mg/dL) with long-term administration of KRN23
* Assess long-term pharmacodynamics (PD) of KRN23 as measured by changes in the following: serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH); serum and urinary phosphorus; ratio of renal tubular maximum phosphate reabsorption rate to glomerular filtration rate (TmP/GFR) and tubular reabsorption of phosphate (TRP); seru

papers.title: Study of KRN23 in Adults With X-linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)
papers.summary: The primary efficacy objective of this study is to establish the effect of burosumab treatment compared with placebo on increasing serum phosphorus levels in adults with XLH.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Burosumab Versus Oral Phosphate and Active Vitamin D Treatment in Pediatric Patients With XLH
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the effect of KRN23 (burosumab) therapy in improving rickets in children with XLH compared with active control (oral phosphate/active vitamin D).

papers.title: A Study of KRN23 in X-linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to assess the safety and tolerability of KRN23 after a single intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in XLH patients.

papers.title: A Repeated Study of KRN23 in Adults With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia
papers.summary: The primary purpose of this study is to assess the safety and efficacy of repeated subcutaneous (SC) injections of KRN23 in adult subjects with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH). A Bone Substudy will evaluate the effects of single-blind KRN23 versus Placebo on bone mineral density and bone quality.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for X-linked hypophosphatemia
Nephrocalcinosis tendency does not worsen under burosumab treatment for X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets: a multicenter pediatric study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective multicenter cohort of 26 children with X-linked hypophosphatemia, burosumab targeting fibroblast growth factor 23 signaling increased serum phosphate and tubular phosphate reabsorption, reduced phosphaturia, alkaline phosphatase, parathyroid hormone, and rickets severity. Hypercalciuria occurred in a small minority, while neither pre-existing nor new nephrocalcinosis was observed to worsen or develop during mean follow-up of 28.4 months.

papers.title: Recurrent Soft Tissue Infections Associated With Burosumab Therapy in X-Linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 57-year-old man with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets who developed recurrent bacterial soft tissue infections during burosumab therapy, with no further infections after treatment discontinuation. The paper proposes that burosumab-mediated disruption of the FGF23-Klotho signaling axis may impair B-lymphocyte-mediated humoral immunity and macrophage-mediated innate immunity, but the causal association remains uncertain because the evidence is from a single case.
papers.why: This XLH case report provides patient-level safety data associating burosumab exposure with recurrent soft-tissue infections that resolved after treatment discontinuation.

papers.title: Effect of burosumab conversion on calciuria and nephrocalcinosis in children with XLH: A real-world cohort study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 13 children with genetically confirmed X-linked hypophosphatemia, conversion to burosumab improved serum phosphate and tubular phosphate reabsorption while suppressing intact parathyroid hormone. A minority developed hypercalciuria or de novo nephrocalcinosis, and the larger parathyroid hormone decline associated with these outcomes was considered hypothesis-generating because of the small, retrospective cohort and sampling limitations.

papers.title: Adolescents' experience of living with X-linked hypophosphataemia (XLH): a mixed-methods analysis of those who continued and discontinued burosumab treatment after end of skeletal growth.
papers.summary: In this 26-week observational study of adolescents with X-linked hypophosphataemia, continued burosumab treatment after the end of skeletal growth was associated with stable serum phosphate and low, stable XLH symptoms. Discontinuation was associated with reduced serum phosphate and, in some patients, worsening pain, stiffness, fatigue, and impacts on physical and social functioning, although substantial missing data and the absence of randomized treatment allocation limit causal conclusions.
papers.why: This study directly evaluates continuation versus discontinuation of burosumab after skeletal maturity and provides patient-reported and biochemical outcomes supporting treatment decisions in XLH.

papers.title: Use of burosumab in McCune Albright syndrome: case report and review of literature in mosaic disorders with FGF23 overproduction.
papers.summary: In a child with McCune-Albright syndrome-associated fibrous dysplasia, burosumab improved phosphate metabolism, reduced alkaline phosphatase and pain, and was not associated with observed adverse events, but it did not stop fibrous-dysplasia progression or reverse femoral deformities. Literature cases in McCune-Albright syndrome and cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome further suggest that the anti-FGF23 antibody improves biochemical and clinical manifestations, with greater skeletal benefit reported in cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome.

papers.title: FGF23-related hypophosphatemic rickets preceding the onset of systemic lupus erythematosus: A juvenile case.
papers.summary: In a single juvenile case, FGF23-related hypophosphatemic rickets preceded juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus, and circulating FGF23 tracked SLE disease activity. Oral sodium phosphate and alfacalcidol accompanied normalization of phosphate, while immunosuppression reduced FGF23, proteinuria, and dsDNA antibodies and was followed by healing of rickets, but the report does not establish a direct therapeutic target for FGF23 signaling.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary patient care in X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets: one challenge, many perspectives.
papers.summary: This review identifies excess FGF23 activity as the central mechanism of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets, causing reduced renal phosphate reabsorption and profound hypophosphatemia. Burosumab binds FGF23, normalizes phosphate excretion, and improves selected skeletal and functional outcomes, while conventional phosphate and active vitamin D treatment remains limited by adverse effects and incomplete control of multisystem disease.

papers.title: Burosumab: First Global Approval.
papers.summary: This review reports that burosumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody directed against fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), increases renal phosphate reabsorption and serum phosphorus and active vitamin D. It summarizes conditional authorization for paediatric XLH, US approval for adults and children aged at least one year, and ongoing or planned evaluation in tumour-induced osteomalacia and epidermal nevus syndrome.

papers.title: Treating 'osteoporosis': a near miss in an unusual case of FGF-23-mediated hypophosphataemic osteomalacia.
papers.summary: This case report identifies an FGF-23-mediated tumour-induced osteomalacia phenotype characterized by hypophosphataemia and renal phosphate wasting, and shows that calcitriol plus phosphate replacement restored phosphate levels and relieved fractures, bone pain, and proximal weakness. It also describes diagnostic assays and reports from the literature that burosumab, an anti-FGF-23 antibody, improves phosphate homeostasis and osteomalacia manifestations in tumour-induced osteomalacia.

papers.title: Mineralized tissues in hypophosphatemic rickets.
papers.summary: This review describes how PHEX mutations elevate osteocyte fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), reducing renal phosphate reabsorption and causing hypophosphatemic rickets, osteomalacia, and dental mineralization defects. It reports that oral phosphate plus calcitriol improves manifestations but incompletely resolves mineralization defects, whereas inactivating FGF23 antibodies provide more stable phosphorus control and appear to heal rickets more reliably, although long-term benefits remain uncertain.

papers.title: Autosomal Dominant Hypophosphatemic Rickets: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
papers.summary: This pediatric case report shows that activating FGF23 variants can cause autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets through excessive FGF23 activity, reduced renal phosphate reabsorption, hypophosphatemia, and impaired mineralization; oral phosphate plus alfacalcidol was followed by biochemical and skeletal improvement, with spontaneous resolution before puberty. The review also identifies Burosumab as an FGF23 inhibitor that reduces phosphaturia and improves rickets in X-linked hypophosphatemia, but states that it had not been studied in autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets.

papers.title: Switching from conventional therapy to burosumab injection has the potential to prevent nephrocalcinosis in patients with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets.
papers.summary: In a retrospective before-and-after study of eight relatively well-controlled children with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets, switching from alfacalcidol plus phosphate to burosumab increased renal phosphate reabsorption and reduced urine calcium extraction without worsening nephrocalcinosis. The findings suggest that burosumab may prevent treatment-associated nephrocalcinosis while maintaining control of disease markers.

papers.title: Expanding the Autosomal Recessive Hypophosphatemic Rickets Type I Carrier Phenotype and Adult Treatment with Burosumab.
papers.summary: This case report expands the phenotype of autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 1 (ARHR1), documenting osteonecrosis of the jaw in an affected adult and subclinical skeletal abnormalities in heterozygous carriers. It also describes treatment with phosphate supplementation, active vitamin D, and burosumab, but the abstract does not provide the direction or magnitude of treatment response.

papers.title: Bone-derived C-terminal FGF23 cleaved peptides increase iron availability in acute inflammation.
papers.summary: In mice with acute inflammation, osteocytes produced most C-terminal FGF23 cleavage peptides, and genetic loss of either osteocyte Fgf23 or osteocyte Furin further lowered circulating iron by increasing hepatic hepcidin. C-terminal FGF23 peptides, delivered systemically or overexpressed in osteocytes, suppressed BMP2/BMP9-induced hepcidin production and preserved iron availability, with no effect on phosphate homeostasis.

papers.title: Osteocyte Egln1/Phd2 links oxygen sensing and biomineralization via FGF23.
papers.summary: The paper identifies osteocyte Egln1/Phd2 as a critical oxygen- and iron-sensitive regulator of FGF23 production. Pharmacologic PHD inhibition increases osteocyte-derived FGF23, whereas HIF1α inhibition or iron repletion suppresses FGF23; these findings provide mechanistically relevant intervention targets for FGF23-driven skeletal disorders.

papers.title: Both enantiomers of β-aminoisobutyric acid BAIBA regulate Fgf23 via MRGPRD receptor by activating distinct signaling pathways in osteocytes.
papers.summary: In mouse osteocytes, L-BAIBA and D-BAIBA both require the MRGPRD receptor to regulate Fgf23, but activate distinct signaling programs: L-BAIBA rapidly increases Fgf23 through Gαs/cAMP/PKA/CBP/β-catenin and Gαq/PKC/CREB, whereas D-BAIBA produces sclerostin through Gαi/NF-κB and subsequently increases Fgf23. Administration of either enantiomer also increased bone Fgf23 in mice under age-, sex-, dose-, and duration-dependent conditions, but this increases rather than suppresses osteocyte FGF23 and therefore is not evidence of a therapeutic approach for X-linked hypophosphatemia.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies Fgf23-expressing osteocytes in response to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 treatment.
papers.summary: In calcitriol-treated C57BL/6J mice, the authors identified a rare osteocyte subpopulation that expressed Fgf23 and showed distinct changes in genes involved in phosphate metabolism and vitamin D response. The study provides a single-cell method and expression markers for resolving Fgf23-producing osteocytes, while showing that calcitriol increases rather than suppresses this relevant cellular mechanism.

papers.title: Mature primary human osteocytes in mini organotypic cultures secrete FGF23 and PTH1-34-regulated sclerostin.
papers.summary: The study developed a long-lived 3D organotypic culture of mature primary human osteocytes that secretes sclerostin and, in some donors, FGF23. Pharmacologic manipulation of sclerostin, mineralization, VEGF, and FGF23 secretion supports the system as a human screening platform for osteocyte-targeting agents, including agents relevant to phosphate-homeostasis disorders such as X-linked hypophosphatemia.

papers.title: Effects of graded phosphate deficiency and vitamin D intervention on growth, bone metabolism, and mineralization in a rat model of neonatal-onset metabolic bone disease.
papers.summary: In neonatal rats, severe neonatal phosphate deprivation caused hypophosphatemia, rickets-like growth-plate widening, reduced bone mineralization, osteopenia, and growth retardation. Supraphysiological vitamin D3 or calcitriol normalized serum phosphate but did not rescue the skeletal mineralization defects and worsened bone loss and growth impairment, indicating that vitamin D monotherapy cannot replace phosphate in this model.

papers.title: Nutritional rickets & osteomalacia: A practical approach to management.
papers.summary: This review identifies defective mineralization of the growth plate as the central skeletal mechanism in nutritional rickets and reports that vitamin D with calcium when needed reverses biochemical and rachitic changes. It also provides transferable diagnostic approaches and preventive interventions, but explicitly warns that phosphate worsens secondary hyperparathyroidism and that calcitriol or alfacalcidol has no role in nutritional rickets.

papers.title: Dental manifestations of hypophosphatasia: translational and clinical advances.
papers.summary: This review describes hypophosphatasia as an ALPL/TNAP deficiency that impairs biomineralization of bones and teeth and summarizes genetic mouse and sheep models, asfotase alfa enzyme replacement therapy, and experimental gene therapies. Asfotase alfa and TNAP-D10 gene-delivery strategies improved mineralized skeletal or dentoalveolar tissues in HPP models, although timing, incomplete rescue, delivery limitations, and weak prospective dental evidence restrict conclusions.

papers.title: Periodic static compression of micro-strain pattern regulates endochondral bone formation.
papers.summary: In rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells carried by HAMA-Alg hydrogels, short-term periodic static compression enhanced proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation, whereas 28-day compression inhibited induced chondrocyte hypertrophy and matrix mineralization. After transplantation into rat femoral condylar defects, combined chondrogenic induction and mechanical loading promoted endochondral bone formation and accelerated bone regeneration, but the induced phenotype was not maintained after ectopic muscle-pouch implantation.

papers.title: Approach to Rickets: Is It Calciopenic or Phosphopenic?
papers.summary: This review describes impaired mineralization of the growth plate as the shared skeletal mechanism of calciopenic and phosphopenic rickets and explains how calcium, phosphate, vitamin D, FGF23, and renal phosphate handling converge on this process. For X-linked hypophosphatemia, PHEX inactivation, elevated FGF23, and renal phosphate loss provide the mechanistic basis for evaluating burosumab, which binds FGF23 and improves phosphate homeostasis and radiographic rickets outcomes.

papers.title: Is it reasonable to ignore vitamin D status for musculoskeletal health?
papers.summary: This review reports that severe vitamin D deficiency, particularly with inadequate calcium intake, can cause rickets and osteomalacia through secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal phosphate wasting, and insufficient calcium or phosphorus for skeletal mineralization. Vitamin D treatment reverses severe deficiency-related musculoskeletal abnormalities, while calcium or combined vitamin D–calcium interventions improve mineralization or fracture outcomes in selected vitamin D–responsive models and susceptible populations.

papers.title: Calcium phosphate polymer induced liquid precursor improves dentin bonding performance of primary teeth with dentinogenesis imperfecta type II.
papers.summary: In an in vitro study using primary molars from patients with dentinogenesis imperfecta type II, calcium phosphate polymer-induced liquid precursor (Ca/P-PILP) increased dentin calcium and phosphorus contents and improved micro-tensile resin-bond strength. The treatment did not normalize the structural defects or bonding strength, and its long-term durability and clinical performance remain unevaluated.

papers.title: scpp5 regulates tooth development and injury-induced repair in zebrafish through mineralization and Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
papers.summary: The study shows that zebrafish scpp5 is required for normal dentin mineralization through Wnt/β-catenin signaling and that scpp5 overexpression promotes dentin repair after tooth injury. Calcium supplementation, pharmacologic Wnt activation, and Wnt10a overexpression partially rescued dentin mineralization defects, whereas Wnt inhibition blocked scpp5-mediated repair; these interventions did not normalize enameloid mineralization.

papers.title: The biphasic concentration-dependent effect of strontium on the mineralization of reconstituted type I collagen and demineralized dentin.
papers.summary: The paper shows that strontium has a biphasic, concentration-dependent effect on mineralization: 0.1–0.5 mM Sr²⁺ enhances dentin remineralization, whereas 0.75–1 mM Sr²⁺ reduces remineralization and intratubular mineral filling. The study also reports enhanced crystal alignment at 0.5 mM Sr²⁺ in reconstituted type I collagen and provides preliminary information for designing strontium-containing biomimetic materials.

papers.title: MG132 facilitates dentin regeneration by modulating inflammation and odontoblast differentiation.
papers.summary: The study reports that local MG132 treatment in a murine pulp exposure model reduces early inflammation and promotes formation of a dentin bridge. In human dental pulp stem cells, MG132 increased Wnt-signaling molecules associated with dentin formation and enhanced odontoblast differentiation and mineralization.

papers.title: In Vitro Odontogenic Differentiation and Mineralisation of Human Dental Pulp Stem Cells Induced by Nano-α-Tricalcium Phosphate/ Silver Nanoparticle Resin Composites for Pulp Capping.
papers.summary: In vitro, nano-α-tricalcium phosphate/silver nanoparticle resin composites were cytocompatible with human dental pulp stem cells and showed mineralization-related activity. The materials increased mineral deposits and induced expression of the odontogenic marker DSPP, although DMP-1 did not show a consistent pattern through day 21; clinical application is not yet supported.

papers.title: A novel approach to full-mouth rehabilitation of dentinogenesis imperfecta type II: Case series with review of literature.
papers.summary: In two sisters with dentinogenesis imperfecta type II, CAD/CAM templates enabled accurate preparation of root post paths and pin holes in obliterated tooth tissues and supported full-mouth rehabilitation with acceptable esthetic and functional results. The intervention restored damaged dentitions but did not correct the underlying dentin hypomineralization, and follow-up identified prosthesis dislodgement and one restoration fracture.

unread.title: [Analysis of PHEX gene mutations in three pedigrees affected with hypophosphatemic rickets].
unread.why: The study directly tested a PCR/Sanger sequencing workflow and identified three causal PHEX variants in XLH pedigrees.

unread.title: Mutational survey of the PHEX gene in patients with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: Direct sequencing of 26 XLH kindreds produced a broad pathogenic PHEX variant spectrum, including a novel 3′-UTR mutation, demonstrating a reusable diagnostic approach.

unread.title: X-linked hypophosphatemia in Polish patients. 1. Mutations in the PHEX gene.
unread.why: The study extends a PHEX mutation catalog to 37 variants and identifies recurrent population-associated mutations useful for XLH genetic diagnosis.

unread.title: Identification of a Novel Pathogenic Variant in the PHEX Gene and Its Mechanistic Implications in X-Linked Hypophosphatemia
unread.why: This XLH case study combines variant functional assays and molecular modelling with real-world use of phosphate and calcitriol and reports biochemical outcomes.

unread.title: Mutational analysis of PHEX gene in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The study validates PHEX mutation detection in familial and nonfamilial XLH and shows that single-strand conformational polymorphism detects more than 60% of mutations.

unread.title: Clinical and genetic analysis in a large Chinese cohort of patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This large XLH cohort validates sequencing, MLPA, structural modelling, and intact FGF23 measurement and identifies mutation-associated biochemical and clinical correlates.

unread.title: Health-related quality of life in French pediatric patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia: real-world data from the International XLH Registry.
unread.why: Registry data from 96 children establish PedsQL instruments and clinical biochemical variables as reusable measures of XLH disease burden and treatment-associated quality of life.

unread.title: Dramatic Transformation After Burosumab in a Young Boy With X-linked Hypophosphatemia: A Life-Changing Saga.
unread.why: The report provides direct clinical evidence that burosumab markedly improved physical function and quality of life in an adolescent with XLH.

unread.title: X-Linked Hypophosphatemia in a Family Cohort: Clinical Variability, Genetic Confirmation and Modern Therapeutic Perspectives.
unread.why: The family cohort provides clinical evidence for PHEX testing, cascade screening, early burosumab treatment, and lifelong multidisciplinary management of XLH.

unread.title: Advancing Patient Evidence in XLH (APEX): Baseline analysis of a global data unification program.
unread.why: APEX unifies three large observational cohorts and provides reusable datasets and longitudinal endpoints for studying XLH progression, treatment effectiveness, and safety.

unread.title: Health-related quality of life in French adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia: real-world data from the International XLH Registry.
unread.why: The study validates use of the SF-36 v2 and International XLH Registry data to measure health-related quality of life and identify clinically associated factors in adults with XLH.

unread.title: Two variants in SLC34A3 in a patient with X-linked hypophosphatemia: a diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma.
unread.why: The case provides a diagnostic strategy using long-read WES/WGS and biochemical discrimination to identify alternative phosphate-handling variants before selecting burosumab in suspected XLH.

unread.title: What are the benefits of the anti-FGF23 antibody burosumab on the manifestations of X-linked hypophosphatemia in adults in comparison with conventional therapy? A review.
unread.why: The review reports quantitative randomized and longitudinal XLH data showing that burosumab corrects hypophosphatemia and improves fracture healing, pain, disability, and bone-remodeling outcomes.

unread.title: Role of prostaglandins in the pathogenesis of X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The study supplies experimental evidence in the PHEX-mutant Hyp mouse that indomethacin can improve the FGF23-associated phosphate transport defect, while its efficacy in patients remains uncertain.

unread.title: Insight into Natural History and Phenotype in Untreated Adults with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This untreated adult XLH cohort provides natural-history data and identifies measurable biochemical and patient-reported outcomes suitable for longitudinal studies and clinical trials.

unread.title: Case Report: Deep intronic <i>PHEX</i> variant causing aberrant splicing identified by whole genome and targeted RNA sequencing in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The case demonstrates an effective diagnostic workflow for genetically unresolved XLH and validates a deep intronic PHEX splice-altering variant using genome and RNA sequencing.

unread.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Burosumab Versus Oral Phosphate and Active Vitamin D in Adults with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH): A 3-Year Follow-Up of the XLH Disease Monitoring Program.
unread.why: Provides three-year real-world evidence comparing burosumab with conventional therapy in adults with XLH and reports phosphate and patient-reported outcomes.

unread.title: Burosumab Therapy in Children with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: A pediatric XLH trial directly demonstrates that burosumab improves phosphate reabsorption, rickets severity, growth, physical function, and pain.

unread.title: Continued Beneficial Effects of Burosumab in Adults with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: Results from a 24-Week Treatment Continuation Period After a 24-Week Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Period.
unread.why: Reports sustained efficacy and safety of continued burosumab treatment in adults with XLH, including phosphate normalization, fracture healing, and functional outcomes.

unread.title: Aberrant Phex function in osteoblasts and osteocytes alone underlies murine X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: Develops conditional and global murine Phex models demonstrating that osteoblast/osteocyte Phex dysfunction is sufficient to produce the XLH phenotype.

unread.title: Circulating levels of soluble klotho and FGF23 in X-linked hypophosphatemia: circadian variance, effects of treatment, and relationship to parathyroid status.
unread.why: Characterizes FGF23 and klotho as measurable disease-associated biomarkers in children and adults with XLH and defines their treatment and circadian behavior.

unread.title: PHEX analysis in 118 pedigrees reveals new genetic clues in hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: Evaluates PHEX mutation screening in familial and sporadic hypophosphatemic rickets and provides a workflow for variant detection and family testing.

unread.title: Impaired 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 action underlies enthesopathy development in the Hyp mouse model of X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: Demonstrates in mechanistically relevant mouse models that impaired vitamin D action causes XLH enthesopathy and that vitamin D or FGF23-directed interventions can prevent it.

unread.title: Two novel variants of the PHEX gene in patients with X‑linked dominant hypophosphatemic rickets and prenatal diagnosis for fetuses in these families.
unread.why: Identifies novel PHEX variants and applies molecular and amniotic-fluid testing for prenatal diagnosis in families with XLH.

unread.title: Sclerostin antibody improves alveolar bone quality in the Hyp mouse model of X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH).
unread.why: The study directly tests sclerostin antibody in Hyp mice and reports improved alveolar bone mass and tissue mineral density with mechanistic beta-catenin measurements.

unread.title: Co-occurrence of Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia and X-Linked Hypophosphatemia in a Three-Generation Chinese Family.
unread.why: The report confirms coexisting COL2A1 and PHEX disorders with sequencing and CNV methods and provides longitudinal radiographic and biochemical evidence for phosphate and calcitriol treatment in XLH.

unread.title: Intragenic duplication of PHEX in a girl with X-linked hypophosphatemia: a case report with review of literature.
unread.why: The study resolves a previously undetected intragenic PHEX duplication and characterizes its structure and X-inactivation status using concrete diagnostic methods in an XLH patient.

unread.title: Burosumab versus conventional therapy in children with X-linked hypophosphataemia: a randomised, active-controlled, open-label, phase 3 trial.
unread.why: This randomized phase 3 trial directly shows that burosumab improves rickets severity, growth, and biochemical outcomes compared with conventional therapy in pediatric XLH.

unread.title: Treatment of X-linked hypophosphatemia with calcitriol and phosphate increases circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 concentrations.
unread.why: This prospective XLH study directly evaluated standard therapy and found that phosphate plus calcitriol was associated with increased circulating FGF23, an important efficacy and safety biomarker.

unread.title: A clinical and molecular genetic study of hypophosphatemic rickets in children.
unread.why: The study reports PHEX/FGF23 testing and clinical outcomes from vitamin D and phosphate treatment in children with hypophosphatemic rickets, including evidence of incomplete efficacy and treatment complications.

unread.title: The elevation of circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 without kidney disease does not increase cardiovascular disease risk.
unread.why: This study develops and validates a PHEX-mutant mouse model reproducing elevated FGF23 and hypophosphatemia while testing cardiovascular phenotypes relevant to XLH.

unread.title: Mutational analysis of PHEX, FGF23, DMP1, SLC34A3 and CLCN5 in patients with hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: The combined sequencing and deletion/duplication assay identified causal variants in a high proportion of patients with hypophosphatemic rickets.

unread.title: Structure and function of disease-causing missense mutations in the PHEX gene.
unread.why: The study experimentally characterizes disease-associated PHEX variants using functional assays for secretion, trafficking, proteolytic activity, and protein conformation.

unread.title: Disease-causing missense mutations in the PHEX gene interfere with membrane targeting of the recombinant protein.
unread.why: The paper tests XLH-associated PHEX mutants in a cell model and evaluates low-temperature rescue and glycerol as potential chaperone strategies for trafficking defects.

unread.title: Functional Characterization of PHEX Gene Variants in Children With X-Linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets Shows No Evidence of Genotype-Phenotype Correlation.
unread.why: The study combines clinical genotyping with functional testing of PHEX variants, providing assays for expression, trafficking, secretion, and catalytic activity in XLH.

unread.title: Risk of cardiovascular involvement in pediatric patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This prospective pediatric XLH cohort establishes monitoring approaches and outcome measures for cardiovascular involvement and reports data on FGF23 and cardiac structure.

unread.title: Genetic and clinical profile of patients with hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: The study validates a genetic and biochemical diagnostic strategy that distinguished PHEX-related and other forms of hypophosphatemic rickets.

unread.title: Bilateral coronal and sagittal synostosis in X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets: a case report.
unread.why: This same-disease case reports a tested surgical approach for craniosynostosis in a child with XLH and describes the age-dependent modifications required.

unread.title: X-linked hypophosphatemia in Polish patients. 2. Analysis of clinical features and genotype-phenotype correlation.
unread.why: The study reports clinical outcomes from phosphate and vitamin D3 supplementation in a 59-person XLH cohort.

unread.title: Meta-analysis and systematic review: burosumab as a promising treatment for children with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This meta-analysis provides efficacy data for burosumab in pediatric XLH, including biochemical and skeletal outcomes.

unread.title: Burosumab Efficacy and Safety in Patients with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Real-World Data.
unread.why: This real-world meta-analysis reports quantitative efficacy and safety outcomes for burosumab across 289 children and adults with XLH.

unread.title: Exome Sequencing in Monogenic Forms of Rickets.
unread.why: Exome sequencing successfully diagnosed multiple monogenic rickets forms, including several PHEX-associated cases, in a 10-family cohort.

unread.title: Switching from active vitamin D and phosphate supplementation to burosumab significantly corrects lower limb malalignment in pediatric X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This multicenter longitudinal study directly shows that switching pediatric XLH patients to burosumab improves lower-limb alignment more than continued active vitamin D and phosphate.

unread.title: Recombinant growth hormone therapy for X-linked hypophosphatemia in children.
unread.why: The systematic review evaluates recombinant growth hormone in children with XLH and reports potential benefits and harms from two controlled studies.

unread.title: Efficacy of Burosumab Every 2 Weeks in an Adult with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: Should We Learn from Children?
unread.why: A case study in adult XLH provides direct evidence that more frequent burosumab dosing improved phosphate reabsorption and biochemical outcomes in a patient inadequately controlled on standard-frequency treatment.

unread.title: A Mild Presentation of X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Caused by a Non-Canonical Splice Site Variant in the PHEX Gene.
unread.why: The study demonstrates genetic and RNA-based diagnostic approaches for identifying and characterizing a mild PHEX splice variant in XLH.

unread.title: Prevalence of enthesopathies in X-linked hypophosphatemia: an explorative ultrasound study.
unread.why: This XLH study establishes ultrasound and functional measures for quantifying enthesopathy, pain, and mobility limitations relevant to disease monitoring and intervention research.

unread.title: Burosumab in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia: real-world experience from a retrospective study in Sydney.
unread.why: A real-world study directly shows burosumab treatment in adults with XLH, including biochemical normalization, WOMAC improvement, dosing management, and adverse-event monitoring.

unread.title: Challenges in Estimating Renal Function in X-linked Hypophosphatemia Because of Formula Overestimation and FGF23 Effects.
unread.why: The study provides evidence that creatinine eGFR overestimates renal function in XLH and supports cystatin C or measured GFR for renal assessment.

unread.title: Improvement in Physical Function Associated With Burosumab in a Patient With X-linked Hypophosphatemia: A Case Report.
unread.why: The case provides direct evidence that burosumab improved objective physical-function measures in an adult with XLH.

unread.title: Case Report: Increased FGF23 and new insufficiency fractures at burosumab discontinuation in X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The report documents burosumab-associated fracture healing and provides clinically relevant data on FGF23 rebound, new fracture, and consequences of treatment discontinuation in XLH.

unread.title: Patient and carer perceptions and acceptability of current management practices in paediatric X-linked hypophosphatemia treated with burosumab therapy.
unread.why: This study evaluates patient and caregiver acceptability of burosumab and identifies telehealth and multidisciplinary-care practices that can support pediatric XLH management.

unread.title: Real-world impact of treatment on growth in children with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: A pooled real-world analysis provides direct evidence that burosumab is associated with improved longitudinal growth outcomes in children and adolescents with XLH.

unread.title: Burosumab improves alkaline phosphatase and rickets severity in X-linked hypophosphatemia: 3-year SUNFLOWER analysis.
unread.why: The three-year SUNFLOWER analysis links burosumab treatment with improved phosphate and bone-metabolism markers and evaluates clinically relevant radiologic, quality-of-life, and functional outcomes in XLH.

unread.title: Contemporary Medical and Surgical Management of X-linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets.
unread.why: Describes medical and surgical management strategies, including osteotomy and guided growth techniques, for bone deformities in X-linked hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Hypocalcaemic and hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: Reviews diagnostic approaches and current therapies for hypophosphatemic rickets, including anti-FGF23 treatment relevant to X-linked hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Burosumab for Pediatric X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: Reports clinical evidence that burosumab improves rickets, growth, pseudofracture healing, and musculoskeletal outcomes in X-linked hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Recombinant growth hormone therapy for X-linked hypophosphatemia in children.
unread.why: Systematic review of controlled trial evidence evaluating growth hormone as an adjunct to standard treatment in children with X-linked hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Real-world effectiveness of burosumab vs oral phosphate and active vitamin D in adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: Provides real-world comparative data showing burosumab improves biochemical, pain, physical-function, and mobility outcomes versus oral phosphate and active vitamin D.

unread.title: Prenatal diagnosis for a novel splice mutation of PHEX gene in a large Han Chinese family affected with X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: Reports a validated molecular workflow for identifying a pathogenic PHEX splice variant and performing prenatal diagnosis in an affected family.

unread.title: 3D-DXA reveals significant effects of burosumab on trabecular and cortical skeletal envelopes in symptomatic adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: Reports a quantitative 3D-DXA method demonstrating that burosumab increases cortical and trabecular bone in symptomatic adults with X-linked hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Postprandial serum phosphorus and calcium concentrations in adults and children with X-linked hypophosphatemia during burosumab treatment.
unread.why: Clinical trial substudy data support nonfasting serum phosphorus as a practical alternative for monitoring stable burosumab-treated patients when fasting is not possible.

unread.title: Real-world effectiveness of burosumab across age groups: X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) Disease Monitoring Program.
unread.why: This prospective real-world study demonstrates sustained biochemical, clinical, and patient-reported benefits of burosumab across XLH age groups and provides a long-term outcomes-monitoring resource.

unread.title: Radicular and periodontal structural defects underlie refractory oral pathology in the adult Hyp mouse model of X-linked Hypophosphatemia
unread.why: The study directly characterizes dental and periodontal disease in a Phex-deficient XLH mouse model using histological and electron-microscopy methods.

unread.title: PHEX Gene Dosage Drives Meniere’s Disease and Related Audiovestibular Phenotypes in X-Linked Hypophosphatemia
unread.why: The study establishes a PHEX genotype–audiometric/radiologic phenotype relationship and provides concrete tests for identifying and monitoring an XLH-associated audiovestibular phenotype.

unread.title: Craniosynostosis in Children with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Treated with Burosumab: Insights from a Single Center Cross-sectional Cohort Screening
unread.why: This pediatric XLH cohort evaluates craniosynostosis and Chiari I malformation screening and supports black-bone MRI as a nonionizing diagnostic alternative to CT.

unread.title: A deep intronic PHEX variant in a large Danish family with hereditary hypophosphatemia and a milder skeletal, but more severe dental phenotype.
unread.why: The report identifies a diagnostically actionable deep-intronic PHEX splice variant and validates its effect with genome and in-vitro exon-trapping methods.

unread.title: Impact of oral phosphate supplements and active vitamin D treatment on dentoalveolar features of X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This study directly tests conventional phosphate plus active vitamin D treatment in an XLH mouse model and in patient teeth, providing evidence about which dentoalveolar outcomes are or are not rescued.

unread.title: X-linked hypophosphatemia in the presence of a <i>CLDN16</i> variant: implications for renal handling and disease severity.
unread.why: This case provides patient-level evidence for burosumab and parathyroid management in severe XLH with a coexisting CLDN16-related renal tubular disorder.

unread.title: Burosumab use in fibroblast growth factor-23-mediated hypophosphatemia in McCune-Albright syndrome/fibrous dysplasia.
unread.why: Burosumab successfully treated FGF23-mediated phosphate wasting in McCune-Albright syndrome-related fibrous dysplasia, supporting transfer to a mechanistically similar FGF23-driven hypophosphatemia.

unread.title: Longitudinal Single-Cell Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Dynamic Immune Cell Alterations During Burosumab Therapy in X-Linked Hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This study provides a reusable longitudinal scRNA-seq workflow and candidate immune-cell biomarkers associated with the response of pediatric XLH to burosumab.

unread.title: Prolonged neonatal phosphate retention and transient hypercalcemia following antenatal Burosumab exposure: a pharmacovigilance alert.
unread.why: The case identifies prolonged neonatal phosphate retention and transient hypercalcemia after antenatal burosumab and provides a monitoring approach for neonatal mineral-metabolism effects.

unread.title: Effects of burosumab on macrophage polarization and TRPV1 expression in children with XLH.
unread.why: Patient cells and direct in-vitro experiments show that burosumab shifts macrophage polarization and reduces TRPV1, identifying potential mechanism and pharmacodynamic biomarkers beyond phosphate correction.

unread.title: Continuation of burosumab during pregnancy in a patient with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: This case supplies real-world evidence and follow-up outcomes for continuing burosumab during pregnancy and managing a PHEX-affected neonate.

unread.title: Burosumab vs Phosphate/Active Vitamin D in Pediatric X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: A Subgroup Analysis by Dose Level.
unread.why: A randomized pediatric XLH trial provides direct comparative efficacy data for burosumab versus phosphate plus active vitamin D, including radiographic and biochemical outcomes.

unread.title: Lessons learned from the real-world diagnosis and management of hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets.
unread.why: The report provides real-world diagnostic and management evidence in PHEX-related XLH and highlights genetic testing and burosumab as reusable clinical approaches.

unread.title: Fibroblast growth factor 23 in oncogenic osteomalacia and X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The study develops and validates an FGF23 immunoassay and shows markedly elevated circulating FGF23 in patients with XLH, supporting biomarker-based diagnosis and management.

unread.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 3 Trial Evaluating the Efficacy of Burosumab, an Anti-FGF23 Antibody, in Adults With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia: Week 24 Primary Analysis.
unread.why: A phase 3 trial directly demonstrates burosumab efficacy in adults with XLH through phosphate normalization, pain and function outcomes, and fracture healing.

unread.title: Pex gene deletions in Gy and Hyp mice provide mouse models for X-linked hypophosphatemia.
unread.why: The paper establishes Hyp and Gy as genetically defined mouse models of X-linked hypophosphatemia that can support mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

unread.title: Prolonged Correction of Serum Phosphorus in Adults With X-Linked Hypophosphatemia Using Monthly Doses of KRN23.
unread.why: Phase 1/2 studies directly test monthly KRN23 in adults with XLH and report sustained phosphate normalization and renal reabsorption improvements.
